scope: Resolve the Actor* cluster opcode gap (16 opcodes in 0x00C9..0x00E3 range observed in pcap but missing from receiver_opcode_map_inbound). The unmapped-s2c-opcode-worklist pass excluded these as `low map/channel opcode range` - that classification was wrong. The 1.23b client dispatches these opcodes through the central s2c dispatcher FUN_004DC690 using a polymorphic per-actor vftable[9] mechanism rather than per-opcode *Receiver classes.

method.step1: Cross-referenced 29 excluded opcodes from manifests/unmapped_s2c_opcode_worklist.json against receiver_opcode_map_inbound.json - confirmed NONE of the 16 0x00C9..0x00E3 cluster opcodes are in the catalog.
method.step3: Catalog scan for prior attributions found BCS-Y-0279 (Option2_central_packet_dispatcher_FUN_004dc690) and BCS-Y-0321 (ZoneOutbound_TierD_HelperBuilt_0x00CA_FUN_004DC690) - same function with CONTRADICTORY interpretations.
method.step4: Decomped FUN_004DC690 (3364 bytes, sole caller FUN_004E20A0 Map tick handler). Confirmed BCS-Y-0279 is correct - it IS the s2c dispatcher with two-branch structure (0x13D<uVar2 high switch + uVar2<0x12E low switch). BCS-Y-0321's `c2s emitter for 0x00CA` interpretation is partially right but mis-frames the function: the `FUN_004E0240(uVar6, 0xCA, 0)` call at decomp line 647 is INSIDE case 7 of the low-switch as a RESPONSE emit, not the function's primary purpose.

dispatcher_model.caller: FUN_004E20A0 (Map tick handler - dispatcher is invoked once per map tick, not from an async packet receive callback)
dispatcher_model.structure: Two-branch opcode switch on uVar2 (the packet opcode at offset +2 of the s2c game-message body)

high_branch.notes: Contains receiver-class dispatch for opcodes already in the catalog via the receiver-discovery pass (BCS-Y-0386 etc.)

tick-style state walk + emits c2s 0xCA via FUN_004E0240(uVar6, 0xCA, 0) at decomp line 647 - this is the response/sync emit BCS-Y-0321 noted, NOT the function's primary purpose
u8-count + 4-byte-each iteration (up to 32 entries via byte count at iVar8+0x10)

GENERIC ACTOR DISPATCH - falls through to switchD_004dc749_caseD_f label - looks up actor by id via FUN_004d9910(param_2), invokes actor->vftable[9](iVar8). This is where ALL the Actor*Packet handling happens - polymorphic per actor class, not per opcode.
AddActor reception - FUN_004d9910 lookup OR FUN_004d90c0 create-if-missing; marks byte at +0x92 = 1 (alive flag); calls FUN_004caf60 to initialize
RemoveActor reception - FUN_004d9910 lookup; if matches alive-player ptr at +0x17838 clears world flags; calls actor->vftable[0](1) which is MSVC destructor-with-delete

low_branch.fallthrough_semantics: FUN_004d9910 is the actor-id-to-actor-ptr lookup. The +0x24 vtable offset = slot 9 (0x24 / 4 = 9). slot 9 is the polymorphic 'apply this s2c packet to me' handler defined per actor subclass.

key_findings.title: Actor* cluster has NO per-opcode receivers - it's polymorphic per actor class
key_findings.detail: The 24-opcode multi-case fallthrough (0x0F, 0xCC, 0xCD, 0xCE, 0xCF, 0xD0, 0xD3-0xE5) covers position, movement, appearance, animation, target, BG props, special graphic, emote - all common per-actor state mutations. Each is dispatched via FUN_004d9910(param_2) actor lookup then actor->vftable[9](packet). The actor's vftable[9] is the per-class polymorphic handler that interprets the packet payload based on opcode. Adding 'per-opcode' receivers for these would be incorrect architecturally - the catalog should document the dispatch MECHANISM, not per-opcode handlers that don't exist.
key_findings.implication: The receiver_opcode_map_inbound concept doesn't fit the Actor* cluster. These need a different catalog category: 'actor-vftable9-dispatched' opcodes. Each opcode is handled by potentially many actor classes (Player, NPC, EventObject etc.) via their respective vftable[9] implementations - the per-opcode-class mapping is N-to-M, not 1-to-1.

key_findings.title: BCS-Y-0279 vs BCS-Y-0321 contradiction resolved
key_findings.detail: Both describe FUN_004DC690. BCS-Y-0279 is fundamentally correct: it IS the central s2c dispatcher. BCS-Y-0321's 'c2s emitter for 0x00CA' framing is partially right but misleading - the 0xCA emit is INSIDE case 7 of the low-switch as a periodic-sync response, not the function's primary purpose. BCS-Y-0321 should be revised to clarify its role as 'the c2s emit site embedded in case 7 of the s2c dispatcher' rather than a standalone c2s emitter.
key_findings.implication: Anyone reading BCS-Y-0321 might think FUN_004DC690 is primarily an emitter; it isn't. Future c2s-only auditing should not include it in pure-emitter inventories. The dispatcher's primary purpose is s2c routing.

key_findings.title: 21 BCS-Y entries have systematic address typos
key_findings.detail: All entries from the earliest cataloguing era have addresses transcribed as 0x000XXXXX instead of 0x004XXXXX (leading 4 -> 0). Affected: BCS-Y-0145, 0297, 0308, 0309, 0311 (47260 -> 447260), 0312, 0313, 0314, 0315, 0316, 0318, 0319, 0321, 0322, 0323, 0325 (fixed in the pcap-grounded-c2s-validation pass), 0326, 0327, 0331. Also BCS-Y-0011/0012/0013 (BF_encrypt/decrypt/set_key - openssl Blowfish primitives in the .text section). The NAMES of these entries contain the correct FUN_004XXXXX VAs in their suffix; only the address field is wrong. Mechanical fix.
key_findings.implication: Catalog lookup tools using address-based queries would miss these entries. Fixing is straightforward (the canonical address is in the name). The pcap-grounded-c2s-validation pass already fixed BCS-Y-0325; this sweeps the remaining 20.
